propositions: Pass-1 context-limit escalation uses only the model-class ladder constant to determine escalation targets, bypassing the run's configured model provider and silently jumping from Bedrock to direct Anthropic.

The _rung_target function compares the rung's provider-inferred form against itself, so its equality check always succeeds when the class table is unconfigured, causing all escalation targets to degrade to bare Anthropic family names.

A Bedrock-qualified primary model escalates to a bare Anthropic id, composing invalid model strings like bedrock:claude-opus-4-8 and causing failures in provider-isolated containers or unbudgeted Anthropic spend.
The one-criterion entry rung retry substitutes a bare model id even when escalation is not needed, because frontier resolves through the default Anthropic ladder without a configured class table.

The fix must thread the run's primary model into _rung_target and drop escalation rungs whose provider differs from the primary's, unless they are the primary's own rung or providers are undeterminable.
Escalation windows keyed on concrete model families must remain unchanged; only escalation targets move from the model-class ladder to the class vocabulary.
